quick.summary: Why a review turns into did you try, and how one slide prevents it.
quick.takeaway: Show the options you dropped, and why.

beats.line: In every review someone asks, did you try a menu? It eats the hour. Why?
They only see your answer. Not the options you already ruled out.
I did try a menu. It hid half the choices.
Then show that. One slide of rejected options.
Each with one line on why it lost.
Won’t showing weaker ideas make me look unsure?
It shows you looked wider than one idea. That builds trust.
We tried a menu and tabs. Here is why buttons won.
Now the hour goes to the design you chose.

quiz.question: Why show rejected options in a design review?
options: It answers did you try before it is asked, and shows your reasoning
It proves the final design has no weak points
It lets stakeholders pick their favourite
It shows how much work you did
quiz.explanation: Seeing what was ruled out and why builds trust and keeps the review on the chosen design.

quiz.question: Showing the options you rejected makes a designer look less confident.
quiz.explanation: It shows the choice was considered, which makes the final design more convincing.
